user.title: New charge controller
user.description:
A charge controller sets the charging current and the number of phases of one charger. It decides from the house power, solar surplus, power limit, electricity price, EMS signal and battery level.

It uses entities that already exist: it **reads** sensors and **writes** two entities of your charger's own integration. A new controller starts in shadow mode: it shows its decisions but writes nothing until you switch on **Control charger** on its device.

The next steps ask for:
1. **Charger outputs**: what the controller sets.
2. **Charger inputs**: what the charger reports.
3. **Charger limits and safety**: fixed values.
4. **House**: house power and the capacity tariff.
5. **Car** (optional): the battery level.
6. **Price and EMS** (optional).
7. **Tuning**: values that rarely need a change.

data_description.name: The name of the controller device, for example where the charger is.
data_description.import_yaml: The EV Load Balancer YAML package is installed. On: the next steps are prefilled with its entities and values, and the new device starts with its settings. Control charger stays off. You check every step before saving.

outputs.title: Charger outputs: what the controller sets
outputs.description: The two entities of your charger's integration that this controller writes to. Nothing is written while Control charger is off. Another charge controller cannot use the same entities.

data_description.current_limit_entity: A number entity in A that limits the charging current, for example the charger's maximum current limit.
data_description.phase_select_entity: A select entity that switches the charger between 1 and 3 phases.

phases.title: Phase options
phases.description: Which option of the phase setting means 1 phase, and which means 3 phases.

inputs.title: Charger inputs: what the charger reports
inputs.description: Sensors of your charger's integration. The controller only reads them.

data_description.connection_entity: Shows whether a car is connected: a Mode 3 sensor (A, B1–D2, E, F), or a binary sensor that is on while a car is connected.
data_description.charger_power_entity: The power the charger delivers now, in W or kW.
data_description.applied_current_entity: The current limit the charger applies now, in A. Not the current the car draws.
data_description.active_phases_entity: The number of phases the charger uses now: 1 or 3, or the same texts as the phase setting.
data_description.max_current_entity: The highest current the charger allows, for example its installation maximum. Until it has a value, the fallback current is the maximum. Never above 32 A.
data_description.charger_energy_entity: Optional. The charger's energy meter in kWh, for the charged-energy sensors. Without it, the energy is calculated from the charging power.

limits.title: Charger limits and safety
limits.description: Fixed values of your charger, and what it gets when something goes wrong. The defaults fit most chargers.

data.failsafe_keeps_phase: Keep the phases on a sensor fault
data.control_off_action: When Control charger is switched off

data_description.min_current_a: The lowest current at which a car charges, usually 6 A. Below it, the controller stops charging.
data_description.voltage_v: The nominal voltage of one phase, usually 230 V.
data_description.current_step_a: The smallest current change the charger accepts.
data_description.widen_small_decreases: Turn on for Alfen chargers: they ignore some decreases of 0.1 A.
data_description.fallback_current_a: The safe current after a sensor fault, and the start current after the car is unplugged.
data_description.fallback_phase: The safe number of phases after a sensor fault, and after the car is unplugged.
data_description.failsafe_keeps_phase: Off (recommended): a sensor fault switches to the fallback phases, so a charger that stops responding is not left on an unintended phase. On: the phases stay as they are.
data_description.control_off_action: What the charger gets once when you switch Control charger off.

household.title: House
household.description: The power of the house, and the peak of your capacity tariff.

data_description.house_power_entity: The grid power of the house without the charger, in W or kW. Negative while exporting. A sensor smoothed over about 15 s works best.
data_description.solar_power_entity: Optional. Shown in the diagnostics only: the controller finds the solar surplus in the house power.
data_description.monthly_peak_entity: Optional. The highest quarter-hour average power of this month (capacity tariff), as a sensor or number entity in W or kW. With Follow monthly peak on, the power limit rises to the peak factor of this value.

car.title: Car (optional)
car.description: With the battery level, the controller stops at a target, charges urgently below an emergency level, and switches Comfort mode to solar. Leave the fields empty without car data.

data_description.car_soc_entity: A sensor with the car's battery level in %.
data_description.car_max_current_a: The highest current per phase that the car accepts.
data_description.car_min_current_a: The lowest current per phase that the car accepts.

price.title: Price and EMS (optional)
price.description: Inputs that allow or limit charging from the grid. Without a price, the price check is skipped.

data_description.price_entity: The import price per kWh. Above Max charging cost, the car does not use the grid.
data_description.price_attribute: Leave empty to use the sensor state. Fill in when the price is an attribute, for example rate_import.
data_description.ems_entity: A power sensor of your EMS: the grid budget for the car in W, or on/off. 0 W blocks the grid.

tuning.title: Tuning
tuning.description: Values that rarely need a change.

data_description.power_update_threshold_w: An increase is written only when it adds at least this much power, so solar ripple causes no writes. Decreases are always written.
data_description.phase_switch_delay_min: After a change to 1 phase, wait this long before going back to 3 phases.
data_description.recalc_interval_s: How often the controller calculates. Mode, setting, connection and phase changes start a calculation at once.
data_description.peak_factor_pct: With Follow monthly peak on, the power limit can rise to this share of the monthly peak.

shared.title: Inputs shared with another controller

error.min_above_max: The min current is higher than the max current.
error.fallback_out_of_range: The fallback current must be between the min and max current.
error.connection_not_mode3: This sensor does not show a Mode 3 state (A, B1–D2, E, F). Pick a Mode 3 sensor or a binary sensor.
error.phase_select_unavailable: The phase setting has no options. Check that the charger is online.
error.current_entity_in_use: Another charge controller already uses this current limit.
error.phase_entity_in_use: Another charge controller already uses this phase setting.
error.capacity_required: Enter the battery capacity when you pick a battery level sensor.
error.car_min_above_max: The car min current is higher than the car max current.
error.attribute_without_price: Pick a price sensor to use a price attribute.
error.price_attribute_missing: The price sensor has no attribute with this name.

charger_not_responding.title: {name}: the charger does not respond
charger_not_responding.description:
The charger did not follow the last 3 writes: its applied current or active phases did not change in time. The controller tries again at each run, and this issue closes when the charger follows again.

Check that the charger is online and that its integration works. To stop the attempts, switch Control charger off.
